paper.title: No-Regret Learning for Stackelberg Equilibrium Computation in Newsvendor Pricing Games

settings.name_in_paper: Newsvendor Pricing Game: follower (retailer) contextual regret
unmapped: Price-setting newsvendor: follower chooses retail price p and order quantity b given wholesale price a (context) chosen by a leader; reward p*min(d,b) - a*b
Linear additive demand Gamma_theta(p) = max(0, theta_0 - theta_1 p) with additive sigma-sub-Gaussian (Gaussian) noise; realized demand fully observed
Follower best-responds via riskless-price upper-bounding surrogate U_B, inducing an approximation error eps_B

algorithms.name: Learning Algorithm for Newsvendor Pricing Game (LNPG)

symbols.aleph_B: positive constant absorbing early-phase (before change point T') regret
symbols.eps_B: worst-case approximation error of the follower's riskless-price best response
symbols.kappa_H: constant in the bound Delta_H(t) <= kappa_H sqrt(log t / t)

conditions: leader plays a pure strategy pi_A
linear additive demand with sigma-sub-Gaussian noise
assumptions of Section 2.x (perishable inventory, fully observed demand, rational greedy follower)

source.label: thm:follower-regret
source.quote: Given pure leader strategy $\pi_A$, the worst-case regret of the follower, $R_B^T(\pi_A)$, as defined in Eq. \eqref{eq:follower-regret} when adopting the LNPG algorithm, is bounded by $R_B^T(\pi_A) \leq \aleph_B + \epsilon_B T - \theta_1 \kappa_H^2 \log^2(T)$, for sufficiently large values of $T$, where $\aleph_B, \epsilon_B, \theta_1, \kappa_H$ are positive real constants in $\mathbb{R}^+$.

results.notes: Linear regret due to approximation error eps_B. The analysis relies on OFUL confidence sets holding w.p. 1-delta, but the theorem is stated without probability qualifier; recorded as expectation. Proof is informal.

conditions: follower best response B(a) in [underline b_a, bar b_a] (optimistic riskless pricing follower)
linear additive symmetric (Gaussian) demand with constant variance
assumptions of Section 2 on the Newsvendor pricing game

source.label: thm:leader-regret
source.quote: Given the pure strategy best response of the follower defined $\mathfrak{B}(a) \in [\underline{b}_a, \bar{b}_a]$ from Eq. \eqref{eq:ba_lower_bound_true} and \eqref{eq:ba_upper_bound_true} respectively, the worst-case regret, $R_A^T(\pi_A)$, from the leader's perspective, as defined in Eq. \eqref{eq:leader-regret-def} when adopting the LNPG algorithm, is bounded by $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T \log(T)})$.

results.notes: Stackelberg regret of leader; game setting marked out of scope. Proof is informal and relies on high-probability confidence sets and polynomial approximation of the inverse CDF.

symbols.eps_hat: penalty tilde a^* tilde B(tilde a^*) - a^* tilde B(a^*) from follower using an alternative best-response proxy

conditions: follower responds with an alternative best-response function tilde B(a)

source.label: cor:alt_br
source.quote: Suppose the follower were to respond with an alternative best-response function $\tilde{\mathfrak{B}}(a)$. As $a^t \to a^*$, ... the Stackelberg regret $R_A^T(\pi_A)$ from Eq. \eqref{eq:leader-regret} would suffer an additive penalty term of $\hat{\epsilon}T$, where $\hat{\epsilon} = \tilde{a}^* \tilde{\mathfrak{B}}(\tilde{a}^*) - a^* \tilde{\mathfrak{B}}(a^*)$.

results.notes: Expression taken from the proof in the appendix (O(sqrt(T log T) + eps_hat T)).
